question.text: The ionization energy of the hydrogen atom is 13.6 eV. The potential energy of the electron in $n=2$ state of hydrogen atom is

solution.text:
Given, $E_{n}=13.6 \mathrm{eV}$
Energy of an electron in $n^{\text {th }}$ state
$E_{n}=\frac{-13.6 z^{2} \mathrm{eV}}{n^{2}}$
$\therefore$ Energy of an electron in $n=2$ state
$E_{2}=\frac{18-6 z^{2}}{(2)^{2}}=-34 e V$
So.
$\begin{aligned}
P E &=2 E_{n=2} \\
&=2 \times(-3.4) \\
&=-6.8 \mathrm{eV}
\end{aligned}$
